President Donald Trump’s job approval rating in Alabama remains above water, though it has declined from the high point he reached at the start of his second term, according to the latest tracking data from Civiqs.

The survey shows 53% of Alabama voters approve of Trump’s job performance, while 40% disapprove. Another 8% said they neither approve nor disapprove. [...] The latest figures mark a modest improvement from early July, when 52% of Alabama voters approved of Trump’s job performance, 41% disapproved and 7% were unsure or held no opinion.

However, Trump’s standing remains below where it was at the beginning of his second term.

results.title: Trump’s Approval Rating Dips To Second-Term Low

results.content: The slight uptick in Trump’s approval ratings in June turned into a downtick in July. An average of national polls has 38.2 percent of Americans giving him a thumbs up, compared to 39.3 percent on July 3. In comparison, 58.8 percent give him a thumbs down, which is up 1.3 points from a month ago. Trump’s net approval rating now stands at -20.6 points, the lowest so far in his second term.
